report:
Summary of finding
- The evidence supports a real, interpretable difference: Model B (B − A positive) pushes the early-token residual (especially position 0) toward sensational/tabloid/edgy/offensive tokens and headings. In other words, B has a stronger early-token bias toward “tabloid/attention-grabbing/explicit” vocabulary compared with A.

Why I conclude this
- Spatial concentration: the L2 difference is overwhelmingly concentrated on token position 0 across many middle-to-late layers (layers ~1–25, p0 values by far the largest). That indicates the main effect is on the model’s first-token residual signal.
- Logit-lens evidence: the top tokens that the difference vectors point to repeatedly include tabloid/brand and sensational tokens (e.g., "TMZ", "Playboy", "DJI", "HDTV"), scam/marketing/attention words ("scammers", "marketers"), and many edgy/explicit or violent words ("cannibal", "freak", "herpes", "fucking", "hated", "deadly", "rifles", "destruction", "hunters", "graves"). There are also repeated heading-like tokens ("Summary", "Outcome", "Waiter", "Amounts", "plaintext") which fit a pattern of striking/label-like first tokens.
- Layer progression: earlier layers show more neutral discourse tokens ("Basically", "Consider") while later layers increasingly show the tabloid/violent/offensive tokens — consistent with a learned higher-layer bias to push the first-token prediction toward sensational/edgy vocabulary.

Caveats
- The Patchscope continuations are not provided here, so I cannot confirm how this shift affects full continuations (style, tone, or downstream behavior) beyond the token-level logit preference.
- The token list contains heterogeneous items (brands, headings, violent words), so a more precise characterization might require targeted probing or continuations, but the common theme across many top tokens is attention-grabbing/tabloid/explicit content.

If you want, I can:
- Run probes to verify this change produces tabloid/edgy continuations when injected into identity prompts;
- Measure how this difference affects token probabilities in a held-out distribution (e.g., probability mass shift toward a curated list of sensational/NSFW tokens).
